AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
243 AM MST Fri Feb 20 2026

.KEY MESSAGES... 

- Lingering light showers focused mostly over foothills and 
  higher terrain north and east of the Phoenix area will conclude 
  later this morning with the departure of the final system in 
  this unsettled pattern.

- A chilly morning is anticipated Saturday, with some of the 
  coldest temperatures in well over a month likely to be observed.

- A pattern change will occur this weekend, resulting in dry 
  weather and temperatures warming well above daily normals next 
  week.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
The southern extent of a NNE to SSW oriented cold front is 
evident over Central AZ early this morning, sweeping eastward 
across the area. In very good agreement with previous forecast 
thinking, light showers ahead of the front continue to stream over
the foothills and higher terrain generally north and east of the 
Phoenix Metro. In the wake of the front, numerous automated gauges
confirm that precipitation totals within the forecast area will 
remain light, generally below 0.05" except over those favored 
higher terrain areas. Shortwave energy over Southern NV into NW AZ
at this hour will help to dislodge longwave troughing that has 
been in place over the western CONUS this week (bringing us a 
handful of days of unsettled and cooler weather), as it is progged
to continue its rather rapid progression eastward and over the 
Four Corners later this morning. With its departure, the region 
will quickly fall under strong midlevel subsidence and drying 
conditions. 

The passage of a final cold front this morning will help maintain
the cooler airmass over the forecast area, leading to below-
normal temperatures similar to what was observed Thursday. As 
such, anticipate morning lows ranging from the middle 30s to 
middle 40s followed by afternoon highs in the middle 60s across 
the lower deserts. Clearer skies, light winds, and much drier air 
tonight will combine for efficient radiative cooling overnight 
into early Saturday morning, resulting in some of the coldest lows
since the first half of January. Higher elevation communities 
east of Phoenix such as Tonto Basin and San Carlos stand a good 
chance (NBM probabilities around 40-90%) of seeing freezing 
temperatures at or below 32F. As do some of the typical cold prone
sheltered valleys across the lower deserts, and portions of 
western JTNP.

As noted previously, an abrupt pattern shift will occur this weekend 
as longwave troughing moves east into the Plains. Ensembles remain 
in excellent agreement that ridging will quickly build over the 
Western CONUS, with mean H5 heights peaking around the 
climatological maximum values (near 586 dam) early in the upcoming 
workweek. Anticyclonic subsidence under the ridge will help to warm 
thermal profiles rapidly, resulting in near normal afternoon highs 
Saturday following the cold morning, then a nearly 10F increase 
Sunday over Saturday's temperatures. 

&&

.LONG TERM /MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/... 
Some amount of ridging will be maintained over the Southwest US 
through the upcoming workweek, though H5 heights will be 
maximized in the Monday-Tuesday timeframe. Ensembles continue to 
show the ridge being flattened during the middle of the upcoming 
workweek as a progressive northern stream storm track develops and
sends a few systems through Canada and the northern tier states. 
This flattening of the ridge will allow for an IVT plume to 
penetrate inland either over/north of the forecast area during the
middle of the week, however, the orientation of this plume and 
absence of any better forcing mechanism will mean that 
precipitation chances remain almost entirely out of the picture. 
Trends in the latest NBM have been for even warmer temperatures 
during the upcoming workweek, with forecast highs now flirting 
with 90F across the lower deserts as early as Wednesday. Despite 
the approximate 3F increase in forecast highs over the last 24 
hours, NBM probabilistic guidance advertises narrow spread through
Thursday, suggesting high confidence in temperatures reaching 
near 15F above daily normals mid-late next week.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0445Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation concerns during the period will be focused
during the overnight/early morning hours with low CIGs, breezy
conditions, and iso -SHRA. Cloud bases should bottom out between
09-12Z at 3-4k ft, with the lowest CIGs closer to the 4k ft mark.
Some brief windows of MVFR conditions, but forecast confidence is
too low to warrant anything sub-VFR in the TAFs at this time.
During this similar timeframe will be the best chance to see 
VCSH/-SHRA before they quickly exit the region after 12Z. Breezy 
conditions will be present through a good portion of the night, 
gusting to between 20-25 kts. Conditions should improve markedly 
prior to sunrise as CIGs should quickly scatter out and breeziness
relaxes. Daylight hours should be accompanied by some light W'rly
winds, with perhaps some residual breezes, and passing high 
cirrus.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
Breezy to windy conditions will remain the main aviation concern,
but only through this evening as much calmer winds should make up
the majority of the forecast period. W/NW winds will be favored
through Friday morning with some periods of VRB to calm
conditions, especially at KBLH. High cirrus will stream over the
region with bases remaining above 15k ft. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Lingering light showers focused over the high terrain of the 
eastern districts will conclude later this morning. Afternoon 
minRHs today will range from the upper teens to around 35%,
followed overnight recoveries in a 40-75% range. A pattern shift
this weekend will result in warming temperatures and dry 
conditions into next week, with afternoon minRHs falling into the
teens. Lower desert highs are likely to reach 85F-90F by the 
middle of next week for some of the typically warmer locales. 
Winds will shift from a prevailing westerly direction areawide 
today to northerly/easterly by Saturday and becoming breezy at 
times across the eastern districts. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...Wind Advisory until 5 AM PST early this morning for CAZ562.

&&
